discovery: Detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies and their establishment as a cosmic standard ruler

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: Will J. Percival
nominees.affiliation: University of Waterloo and Perimeter Institute, Canada

motivation: In 2005 two independent analyses, of the SDSS luminous red galaxies (led by Eisenstein) and of the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (led by Cole and Percival), detected the imprint of sound waves in the primordial baryon-photon plasma on the clustering of galaxies. This linked the acoustic peaks of the cosmic microwave background to the late-time Universe. Eisenstein also did much of the theory that turned the BAO feature into a robust standard ruler, including the transfer-function calculations and density-field reconstruction. Percival and Cole developed the statistical methods that made the measurement reliable. Because the BAO scale is set by well-understood linear physics, it is unusually insensitive to systematics. That property made it the geometric backbone of BOSS, eBOSS, DESI and Euclid. It independently confirmed cosmic acceleration and now gives the sharpest test of whether dark energy is a cosmological constant, including DESI's recent hints of evolving dark energy.
